statusText: Roughly four hours after the U.S. cash open (about 1:30pm ET): the confirmed August UMich consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM) remain fully priced. Index-level reporting this hour is more consistently negative than last hour's mixed reads: the S&P 500 was down about 0.21% to 7,782.65 and the Nasdaq Composite down about 0.50% as of 11:39am ET, with the Nasdaq-100 reported off roughly 0.4%, a day after Thursday's record S&P 500 close above 7,800 -- still a modest, contained pullback rather than a confirmed directional break. NQ futures have not produced a fresh confirmed intraday quote this hour (most live-data financial sites were blocked by the network egress proxy and Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota was exhausted after three calls), so the last confirmed session range remains 30,124.25-30,232.00 under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall; no failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure has been observed in NQ itself. VIX holds calm near 14.5 (today's range about 14.48-14.65). 2Y/10Y Treasury yields (4.20%/4.68%) and QQQ ($732.07) remain unchanged from Alpha Vantage's stale prior reads (dated August 12-13). WTI trades in an $80.77-$82.99 range (~$81) and Brent is little changed near $87.18 (+0.13%), consistent with continued digestion of the Strait of Hormuz situation. A UKMTO advisory today confirmed a further drone attack on an oil tanker exiting the Strait of Hormuz (minor damage, no casualties, no oil spill), extending the near-standstill transit backdrop already flagged last hour rather than representing a fresh major escalation; oil has not broken out of its recent range in response. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD (2Y, 10Y) and GLOBAL_QUOTE (QQQ) calls succeeded but returned the same unchanged stale prints as prior runs; WTI/BRENT/MARKET_STATUS calls were rate-limited (25-request daily quota exhausted) and not retried further per the economical-use instruction. Live VIX, index-level percentage moves, oil pricing, and the Hormuz tanker-attack detail all came from WebSearch, since most primary financial-data sites (Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, CNBC, Barchart, TheStreet, Benzinga) returned an egress-proxy block on direct fetch this run.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail holds low because NQ itself continues to show no persistent one-way structure -- the last confirmed session range is unchanged and no fresh intraday quote this hour showed a failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction, despite today's confirmed data misses and the newly confirmed (but UKMTO-classified as minor) Hormuz tanker drone attack. Stress holds roughly flat versus the prior run in the upper-moderate band: the UMich/Retail Sales surprise is further behind the tape, but the fresh, corroborated Hormuz drone-attack confirmation is a genuine, if still contained, event-importance driver that offsets the natural decay from the data prints alone. Confidence eases from the prior run because Alpha Vantage's free-tier quota was exhausted this run and most direct financial-data fetches were blocked, leaving this hour's assessment more reliant on WebSearch snippets than usual. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself -- not the standing data misses, the Hormuz drone attacks/rhetoric on their own, or any single-stock catalyst.
headline: Confirmed UMich miss and already-absorbed Retail Sales drop stay digested as major indices ease a modest, more consistently negative 0.2-0.5% lower into early afternoon; a fresh UKMTO-confirmed drone attack hit a tanker exiting the Strait of Hormuz today, but VIX (~14.5) and oil (WTI ~$81, Brent ~$87) remain little changed and NQ's last confirmed range is unchanged.
body: At 17:30 UTC, roughly four hours after the U.S. cash open, the confirmed August University of Michigan consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM vs +0.1% expected) remain fully digested. Index-level reporting this hour is more consistently negative than the prior run's mixed reads: as of 11:39am ET the S&P 500 was down about 0.21% to 7,782.65 and the Nasdaq Composite down about 0.50% to 26,664.30, with separate reporting placing the Nasdaq-100 off roughly 0.4% and the Dow down about 0.2%, a day after Thursday's record S&P 500 close above 7,800. This is a modest, contained give-back rather than a confirmed directional break. NQ futures produced no fresh confirmed intraday quote this hour: most primary live-data financial sites (Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, CNBC, Barchart, TheStreet, Benzinga) returned an egress-proxy block on direct fetch, and the WebSearch-returned NQ figures this hour were either a repeat of the prior run's timestamped print or an inconsistent late-day figure not clearly dated to today, so neither was treated as a fresh confirmed observation. The last confirmed session range therefore remains 30,124.25-30,232.00, still under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall, with no observed failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure. VIX remains calm, near 14.5 (today's reported range about 14.48-14.65). Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD calls (2Y 4.20%, 10Y 4.68%, both dated August 12) and GLOBAL_QUOTE (QQQ $732.07, dated August 13) succeeded this run but returned the identical stale values already published in prior runs; the subsequent WTI call was rate-limited (Alpha Vantage's 25-request daily quota, shared across today's hourly runs, is now exhausted) and, per the economical-use instruction, was not pursued further after one retry -- BRENT and MARKET_STATUS were not attempted. Oil pricing therefore came from WebSearch: WTI trading in an $80.77-$82.99 range (opened ~$81.12) and Brent little changed near $87.18 (+0.13% from the prior close), consistent with continued rangebound digestion of the Strait of Hormuz situation. A UKMTO maritime security advisory issued today (Friday, August 14) confirmed a further drone attack on an oil tanker exiting the Strait of Hormuz, with minor damage, all crew safe, and no oil spill reported; this extends -- but does not clearly intensify beyond -- the near-standstill transit backdrop already flagged in the prior run's confirmed Thursday-evening tanker attacks and U.S. blockade/'economic isolation' rhetoric. Oil has not broken out of its recent range in response, so this is treated as a continuing Stress driver rather than a Tail driver. In single-stock news, Reddit extended its gain (up as much as 10-14% intraday across sources) ahead of joining the S&P 500 on August 18, and Globant sank about 12.6% on disappointing Q2 earnings; neither is an index-level one-way catalyst. Tail holds at 8% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- the last confirmed NQ range is unchanged and today's more consistently negative but still sub-1% cross-index reaction does not show failed-pullback or repeated-extension behavior. Stress holds at 41% (moderate, upper band), essentially flat versus the prior run's 42%, because while the UMich/Retail Sales surprise is further behind the tape, the freshly confirmed Hormuz drone-attack detail is a genuine, corroborated event-importance driver that offsets the natural decay from the data prints alone. Confidence eases to 45% (medium-low) from the prior run's 52% because Alpha Vantage's daily quota was exhausted after three repeat-stale calls this run, and most direct financial-data site fetches were blocked by the network egress proxy, leaving this hour's index-level and NQ-specific evidence more reliant on WebSearch snippets -- with some genuine corroboration across independent searches for the equity-index moves, VIX, oil and the Hormuz detail, but no fresh confirmed NQ intraday quote.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (8-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing steadily from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion into a stable single-digit floor through Friday's Asian/European session, then holding 8-9% through today's confirmed UMich and Retail Sales misses into the early U.S. afternoon. Stress ran from the upper-30s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, then rebuilt steadily through the European morning and into the confirmed UMich print, peaking at 44% before easing modestly and then holding flat around 41-42% as the data digested further without a confirmed equity-market breakdown; the newly confirmed Strait of Hormuz tanker/drone attacks (Thursday evening and again today) add a persistent, if still contained, event-importance driver to the current read.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-8%) through the next 24 hours as no confirmed persistent one-way NQ structure is in evidence and no further high-impact U.S. data is scheduled before the Friday close. Stress is projected to resume easing from today's flat-to-slightly-lower moderate band as the UMich/Retail Sales data and the confirmed-but-contained Hormuz tanker/drone-attack headlines are further digested through the remainder of the U.S. session, dropping toward the low-teens by the ~21:00-22:00 UTC Friday close/CME weekend halt for NQ. From roughly 22:00 UTC Friday through the end of this forecast window (16:00 UTC Saturday), NQ futures are closed for the CME weekend break (reopening Sunday ~22:00 UTC), so Tail and Stress are held near a low weekend baseline reflecting the absence of active price-path evidence and standing weekend headline/gap risk (principally the Hormuz standoff) rather than any newly observed structure. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the mid-40s toward the high-20s as the horizon moves away from this run's evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
